Messages.Author: devilwithcape
Messages.Body:
I'm sorry if this has already been answered, but I couldn't find it on
here. Anyway, if a player is being bleed for 3 and he plays two
Telepathic Counters at AUS and reduces it by 4 can he reserve the
right to block until his predator increases the bleed to a positive
amount? Or, does he have to declare whether or not he will block
after reducing the bleed (giving his predator the ability to increase
the bleed without fear of it being blocked)?

Messages.Author: YY
Messages.Body:
On Dec 11, 11:05 am, devilwithcape


There is no "reserves the right to block" in Vtes. See [2].

1. If the TC was played after the "choose blockers" window, then the
bleed cannot be blocked. Otherwise, see point [2]

2. If the acting minion passes on playing any more cards, the target
player will have to declare if xe wishes to block (with minion X) or
decline to block (or play more reaction cards).
If xe declines to block, xe cannot attempt to block later, even if the
acting minion increases the bleed.

-YY

Messages.Author: Azel
Messages.Body:


yup, that's why it's best to reduce after "Decline to Block" and not
before.

"Declining to Block" is a declared part of the action process, crucial
to determine resolution, and therefore pretty much cannot be avoided
(barring card text). an action reaches resolution when both players
pass on playing more cards and either success or failure (such as
being blocked) occurs. the reacting player who can legally block
always has a "Decline to Block" declaration that must be processed
before resolving the action. therefore the acting player can
continually pass until that declaration is made. that "Decline to
Block" declaration then grants another chance to play more action
modifiers -- however it is essentially the "last window" for the
acting minion. this is because if he passes after the "Decline to
Block" declaration(s) then the reacting methuselah(s) can just pass
and the action thus moves into resolution.

there's no "pass, pass, play, okay -- now resolve" it's "pass, pass,
resolve." but since meths with legal blocking minions continually
retain blocking declarations, they must explicitly decline further
blocking declarations before they get to move into "pass, pass,
resolve."

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
> yup, that's why it's best to reduce after "Decline to Block" and not
> before.

Azel,
I'll have to disagree with you there. Playing bleed reduce before the
block forces them to expend +bleed on an action that might just get
blocked anyway. Plus it also means that if they have a big handful of
stealth, they don't get that extra cycle they were hoping for. I find
the biggest advantage of Reduction is against S&B. It denies the
predator the ability to cycle stealth and still protects you against
the bleeds.

No, it doesn't.

A: Bleed for 1.
A: Do you block? (i.e, "pass")
B: Reduce by 1: bleed of 0.
A: Do you block? (i.e., "pass")
B: No block.
A: Conditioning: bleed of 3.

> Plus it also means that if they have a big handful of
> stealth, they don't get that extra cycle they were hoping for.

Well, that's what not blocking does. Playing bleed reduction (before or after
declining to block) doesn't affect that (except that it makes it less painful to
decline blocks, sure).
